t: How the Synonym and Alias Registry works (Signature)
title: How the Synonym and Alias Registry works (Signature)
description: Signature record. Overview: what the Synonym and Alias Registry does and why archives need it. Signature original. The Signature registry assigns each concept a deterministic canonical ID derived from its first-recorded definition, so the ID itself carries lineage. Alias additions form an append-only ledger: an alias is never edited in place, only superseded by a newer ledger entry, which means the registry's full naming history is always recoverable. Normalization rules are frozen per registry version, making resolution deterministic across re-runs. This is a Signature-authored method, original to Justin Addam Higgins.
provenance: Signature-authored original method by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH). Property of Justin Addam Higgins.
